runs.t: CQRS separates write-side commands that enforce business rules from read-side queries optimized for retrieving information. It does not inherently require different databases or event sourcing.

Maintain clear write invariants while shaping read models for actual query needs. The split can be logical within one codebase; separate projections only when query complexity or scale justify asynchronous synchronization.
A booking command checks overlap and commits a reservation; a dashboard query joins guest, revenue and availability data without exposing write-model internals. A read replica is optional.
Separate read databases add synchronization lag, deployment work and reconciliation paths. CQRS is not a performance cure if inefficient SQL or incorrect indexing is the actual problem.
